chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from one who narrated to him from Yahya ibn Sa'id from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a woman who fell from the mount and was injured, and could not manage the throwing of the Jamarat. He said: 'She is thrown for, and the unborn child is thrown for.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who cannot throw the Jamarat due to injury or pregnancy during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of vicarious performance (niyabah) for those physically incapacitated during Hajj, specifically addressing a woman who fell from her mount. The ruling extends the obligation to include the unborn child, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the fetus bears ritual responsibilities from the mother, ensuring the completeness of the pilgrimage rites despite temporary disability.
